      "title": "Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET",
      "body": "Both unsubscribe routes use GET, but TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately changes the authenticated user's notification level without an authorization token or confirmation. Rails CSRF protection does not validate GET requests, and this action also skips check_xhr. An external site can therefore send an authenticated user to a predictable unsubscribe URL and demote or mute a topic without consent. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST, or require a signed, recipient-scoped unsubscribe token."

      "body": "This route only loads the ordinary topic view with PostStream.loadTopicView; it never invokes the unsubscribe action or changes the notification level. Following an internal unsubscribe link in an already-running application therefore bypasses the server-side HTML request that performs the mutation. The page says notifications will stop even though the user remains subscribed. Perform the unsubscribe explicitly through a client action rather than relying exclusively on a full-page request."

This action does not create a per-topic record before dereferencing tu.notification_level, so an otherwise valid unsubscribe request fails with NoMethodError and a 500 response. Handle the missing record using the regular notification level as the default and create the preference through TopicUser.change."

findings.title: Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET
findings.body: Both unsubscribe routes use GET, but TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately changes the authenticated user's notification level without an authorization token or confirmation. Rails CSRF protection does not validate GET requests, and this action also skips check_xhr. An external site can therefore send an authenticated user to a predictable unsubscribe URL and demote or mute a topic without consent. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST, or require a signed, recipient-scoped unsubscribe token.

findings.title: Perform the unsubscribe when navigating through Ember
findings.body: This route only loads the ordinary topic view with PostStream.loadTopicView; it never invokes the unsubscribe action or changes the notification level. Following an internal unsubscribe link in an already-running application therefore bypasses the server-side HTML request that performs the mutation. The page says notifications will stop even though the user remains subscribed. Perform the unsubscribe explicitly through a client action rather than relying exclusively on a full-page request.

findings.title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never interacted with the topic, such as someone following a forwarded notification email. This action does not create a per-topic record before dereferencing tu.notification_level, so an otherwise valid unsubscribe request fails with NoMethodError and a 500 response. Handle the missing record using the regular notification level as the default and create the preference through TopicUser.change.

findings.title: Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change
findings.body: Saving notification_level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged. For a regular or automatically tracked TopicUser whose reason is nil, TopicUser.update_last_read changes the level to tracking once the viewed-time threshold is exceeded, even if this action just set it to muted. Reading the topic can therefore silently undo the unsubscribe. Use TopicUser.change so the preference is marked user_changed, its timestamp is updated, and the notification-level change is published.

findings.title: Preserve unsubscribe footers for callers without a topic URL
findings.body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder does not provide a default for it. The previously supported call Email::MessageBuilder.new(to, body: 'hello', add_unsubscribe_link: true) now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the body or HTML footer. Generic callers should still be able to add the preferences link without having a topic URL. Append the topic-specific stanza only when unsubscribe_url is supplied.
